Playbook.name: Windows — Execution via Microsoft DotNet ClickOnce Host - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: rundll32.exe invoked the ClickOnce host (dfshim ShOpenVerbApplication) followed by a network connection within 5s - ClickOnce deployment can run remote .NET applications with limited prompts. Triage question: is this a malicious ClickOnce app, or a legitimate ClickOnce deployment? (This detection exists as a duplicate rule pair; one playbook covers both.)
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: ClickOnce lets an attacker deliver and run a .NET payload from a URL with minimal user friction.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: ClickOnce host
Signal.Details: rundll32 dfshim ShOpenVerbApplication then a network connection.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the ClickOnce execution delivered a malicious app or a legitimate deployment.

Step.name: ClickOnce invocation and network destination
Step.Purpose: The command and the network destination reveal the source of the ClickOnce app.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)rundll32(.exe)?" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*dfshim*" AND (cl LIKE "*shopenverbapplication*" OR cl LIKE "*#*") | KEEP @timestamp, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A ClickOnce app launched from a browser/email link pointing at an external/untrusted URL is the risk. An internal LOB ClickOnce app from a known deployment URL is benign. The parent (browser/outlook) and the deployment URL matter.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: ClickOnce app launched from an external/untrusted URL, especially via a browser/email link, followed by suspicious child activity.
An internal line-of-business ClickOnce app from a known deployment source.
ClickOnce execution with an unclear source URL.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CLICKONCE-DETAIL, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the app; close as benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: Delivery of a malicious .NET application via ClickOnce.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; capture the ClickOnce manifest/payload; open IR.
Block the source; hunt for other recipients.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A vendor app using ClickOnce updates by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
